title.en: Volume 69 Book of Later Tang 45: Biographies 21: Zhang Xian, Wang Zhengyan, Hu Zhuang, Cui Yisun, Meng Hu, Sun Yue, Zhang Yanlang, Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang
title.raw: 卷六十九 唐書45: 列傳21 張憲 王正言 胡裝 崔貽孫 孟鵠 孫岳 張延朗 劉延皓 劉延朗 Volume 69 Book of Later Tang 45: Biographies 21: Zhang Xian, Wang Zhengyan, Hu Zhuang, Cui Yisun, Meng Hu, Sun Yue, Zhang Yanlang, Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang

sentences.zh: 張憲，字允中，晉陽人，世以軍功為牙校。

translations.literal: Zhang Xian, styled Yunzhong, was a man of Jinyang; for generations his family had held the rank of yaxiao through military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian, styled Yunzhong, was a native of Jinyang. For generations his family had risen through military service to the rank of yaxiao.

sentences.zh: 憲始童丱，喜儒學，勵志橫經，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: From his earliest childhood Xian delighted in Confucian learning, resolved to master the classics horizontally, and did not rest day or night.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Xian delighted in Confucian learning, applying himself to mastering the classics day and night without respite.

sentences.zh: 太原地雄邊服，人多尚武，恥於學業，惟憲與里人藥縱之精力遊學，弱冠盡通諸經，尤精《左傳》。

translations.literal: Taiyuan lay in a powerful frontier region; its people mostly honored martial affairs and were ashamed of scholarly study. Only Xian and a townsman, Yao Zongzhi, devoted their energies to travel and study. By weak-capping he had thoroughly mastered all the classics, especially the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan lay in a powerful frontier region where men prized martial prowess and looked down on scholarly pursuits; only Xian and a townsman named Yao Zongzhi devoted their energies to travel and study. By his weak-capping year he had mastered all the classics, with particular mastery of the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 嘗袖行所業，謁判官李襲吉，一見欣歎。

translations.literal: Once he carried his recent work in his sleeve and called on the judge Li Xiji, who at a single meeting expressed delighted admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Once he carried his writings in his sleeve and called on the judge Li Xiji, who at a single meeting expressed delighted admiration.

sentences.zh: 既辭，謂憲曰：「子勉之，將來必成佳器。」

translations.literal: When he took his leave, he said to Xian, "Apply yourself diligently—you will surely become an outstanding vessel in time."
translations.idiomatic: When Xian took his leave, Li said to him, "Apply yourself diligently—you will surely become an outstanding talent in time."

sentences.zh: 石州刺史楊守業喜聚書，以家書示之，聞見日博。

translations.literal: The prefect of Shizhou, Yang Shouye, loved to collect books and showed him his family library, so his knowledge and experience broadened day by day.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Shizhou, Yang Shouye, loved to collect books and showed him his family library, so his learning broadened day by day.

sentences.zh: 莊宗為行軍司馬，廣延髦俊，素知憲名，令朱守殷齎書幣延之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong served as acting commander on campaign, he widely extended invitations to eminent talents, had long known Xian's name, and ordered Zhu Shouyin to bring letters and gifts to invite him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong served as acting commander on campaign, he widely gathered eminent talents and, knowing Xian's reputation by name, had Zhu Shouyin bring letters and gifts to invite him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，釋褐交城令，秩滿，莊宗嗣世，補太原府司錄參軍。

translations.literal: After more than a year he left the white collar as magistrate of Jiaocheng; when his term ended and Zhuangzong succeeded to the succession, he was appointed recorder in the Taiyuan prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he left the white collar as magistrate of Jiaocheng; when his term ended and Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne, he was appointed recorder in the Taiyuan prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 時霸府初開，幕客馬鬱、王緘，燕中名士，盡與之遊。

translations.literal: At that time the chief's headquarters had just been opened; the staff members Ma Yu and Wang Jian, both celebrated names from Yan, all associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chief's headquarters had just been opened; the staff members Ma Yu and Wang Jian, both celebrated names from Yan, all associated with him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，莊宗平河朔，念藩邸之舊，征赴行台。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Zhuangzong pacified Hebei and, mindful of old ties from the princely residence, summoned him to the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Zhuangzong pacified Hebei and, mindful of old ties from the princely residence, summoned him to the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 十三年，授監察，賜緋，署魏博推官，自是恒簪筆扈從。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed surveillance censor, granted scarlet robes, and made investigating officer for Weibo; from then on he constantly wore the brush and followed in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed surveillance censor, granted scarlet robes, and made investigating officer for Weibo; from then on he constantly wore the brush and followed in attendance.

sentences.zh: 十五年，王師戰胡柳，周德威軍不利，憲與同列奔馬北渡；

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the imperial army fought at Huliu; Zhou Dewei's army fared ill, and Xian fled north across the river with his colleagues on horseback;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the imperial army fought at Huliu; Zhou Dewei's army fared ill, and Xian fled north across the river with his colleagues on horseback;

sentences.zh: 梁軍急追，殆將不濟。

translations.literal: The Liang army pressed in pursuit and he was nearly unable to cross.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang army pressed in pursuit and he was nearly unable to cross.

sentences.zh: 至晚渡河，人皆陷水而沒，憲與從子朗履冰而行；

translations.literal: Toward evening they crossed the river; many men sank in the water and drowned. Xian and his nephew Lang walked on the ice;
translations.idiomatic: Toward evening they crossed the river; many men sank in the water and drowned. Xian and his nephew Lang walked on the ice;

sentences.zh: 將及岸，冰陷，朗泣，以馬箠引之，憲曰：「吾兒去矣，勿使俱陷。」

translations.literal: As they neared the bank the ice gave way. Lang wept; Xian pulled him with a riding crop and said, "My boy, go on—do not let us both fall in."
translations.idiomatic: As they neared the bank the ice gave way. Lang wept; Xian pulled him with a riding crop and said, "My boy, go on—do not let us both fall in."

sentences.zh: 朗曰：「忍季父如此，俱死無恨。」

translations.literal: Lang said, "How could I bear my uncle like this? Dying together leaves no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Lang said, "How could I bear to leave my uncle like this? Dying together leaves no regret."

sentences.zh: 朗偃伏引箠，憲躍身而出。

translations.literal: Lang lay prostrate and held out the crop; Xian leapt free.
translations.idiomatic: Lang lay prostrate and held out the crop; Xian leapt free.

sentences.zh: 是夜，莊宗令於軍中求憲，或曰：「與王緘俱歿矣！」

translations.literal: That night Zhuangzong ordered a search for Xian in the army; someone said, "He perished together with Wang Jian!"
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhuangzong ordered a search for Xian in the army; someone said, "He perished together with Wang Jian!"

sentences.zh: 莊宗垂涕求屍，數日，聞其免也，遣使慰勞。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong wept and sought his corpse; after several days word came that he had escaped, and he sent an envoy to comfort and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong wept and sought his corpse; after several days word came that he had escaped, and he sent an envoy to comfort and reward him.

sentences.zh: 尋改掌書記、水部郎中，賜金紫，曆魏博觀察判官。

translations.literal: Soon he was made chief secretary and director in the Ministry of Works, granted gold and purple, and served in succession as investigating officer for the Weibo surveillance commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made chief secretary and director in the Ministry of Works, granted gold and purple, and served in succession as investigating officer for the Weibo surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 從討張文禮，鎮州平，授魏、博、鎮、冀十郡觀察判官，改考功郎中，兼御史中丞，權鎮州留事。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Zhang Wenli; when Zhenzhou was pacified he was appointed investigating officer for the ten prefectures of Wei, Bo, Zhen, and Ji, then promoted to director in the Bureau of Merit, concurrently made vice censor-in-chief, and given charge of Zhenzhou as acting administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Zhang Wenli; when Zhenzhou was pacified he was appointed investigating officer for the ten prefectures of Wei, Bo, Zhen, and Ji, then promoted to director in the Bureau of Merit, made concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and given charge of Zhenzhou as acting administrator.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，詔還魏都，授尚書工部侍郎，充租庸使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was ordered back to the Wei capital, appointed vice minister of works in the Secretariat, and made commissioner of the transport and corvée tax.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was ordered back to the Wei capital, appointed vice minister of works in the Secretariat, and made commissioner of the transport and corvée tax.

sentences.zh: 八月，改刑部侍郎，判吏部銓，兼太清宮副使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was transferred to vice minister of punishments, given charge of civil-service selection in the Ministry of Personnel, and made deputy commissioner of the Taiqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was transferred to vice minister of punishments, given charge of civil-service selection in the Ministry of Personnel, and made deputy commissioner of the Taiqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遷洛陽，以憲檢校吏部尚書、興唐尹、東京副留守，知留守事。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong moved to Luoyang, Xian was made acting minister of personnel, prefect of Xingtang, deputy eastern capital intendant, and given charge of the intendant's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong moved to Luoyang, Xian was made acting minister of personnel, prefect of Xingtang, deputy eastern capital intendant, and given charge of the intendant's affairs.

sentences.zh: 憲學識優深，尤精吏道，剖析聽斷，人不敢欺。

translations.literal: Xian's learning was superior and profound; he was especially skilled in administrative practice, dissecting cases in judgment and hearing, and no one dared deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's learning was superior and profound; he was especially skilled in administrative practice, dissecting cases in judgment and hearing, and no one dared deceive him.

sentences.zh: 三年春，車駕幸鄴，時易定王都來朝，宴於行宮，將擊鞠。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the imperial carriage visited Ye; at that time the Prince of Yiding, Wang Du, came to court, and a banquet was held in the traveling palace with cuju to follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the emperor visited Ye; at that time the Prince of Yiding, Wang Du, came to court, and a banquet was held in the traveling palace with cuju to follow.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗行即位之禮，卜鞠場吉，因築壇於其間，至是詔毀之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhuangzong performed the accession rites, divination had shown the cuju ground to be auspicious, so an altar was built there; now an edict ordered it destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhuangzong performed the accession rites, divination had shown the cuju ground to be auspicious, so an altar was built there; now an edict ordered it destroyed.

sentences.zh: 憲奏曰：「即位壇是陛下祭接天神受命之所，自風燥雨濡之外，不可輒毀，亦不可修。

translations.literal: Xian memorialized, "The accession altar is where Your Majesty sacrificed to receive Heaven's mandate; apart from wind-drying or rain-soaking, it must not be casually destroyed, nor may it be repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Xian memorialized, "The accession altar is where Your Majesty sacrificed to receive Heaven's mandate; apart from wind-drying or rain-soaking, it must not be casually destroyed, nor may it be repaired.

sentences.zh: 魏繁陽之壇，漢汜水之墠，到今猶有兆象。

translations.literal: The altar at Fanyang in Wei and the mound at Sishui in Han still show traces to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The altar at Fanyang in Wei and the mound at Sishui in Han still show traces to this day.

sentences.zh: 存而不毀，古之道也。」

translations.literal: Preserving without destroying is the way of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Preserving without destroying is the way of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 即命治之於宮西。

translations.literal: He was immediately ordered to restore it west of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately ordered to restore it west of the palace.

sentences.zh: 數日，未成。

translations.literal: After several days it was still unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: After several days it was still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 會憲以公事獲謫，閣門待罪，上怒，戒有司速治行宮之庭，礙事者畢去，竟毀即位壇。

translations.literal: It happened that Xian was demoted for an official matter and waited at the gate for punishment. The emperor was angry and ordered the authorities to quickly prepare the traveling palace courtyard; whatever obstructed the matter was removed, and in the end the accession altar was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Xian was demoted for an official matter and waited at the gate for punishment. The emperor was angry and ordered the authorities to quickly prepare the traveling palace courtyard; whatever obstructed the matter was removed, and in the end the accession altar was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 憲私謂郭崇韜曰：「不祥之甚，忽其本也。」

translations.literal: Xian privately told Guo Chongtao, "This is most inauspicious—neglecting the root."
translations.idiomatic: Xian privately told Guo Chongtao, "This is most inauspicious—neglecting the root."

sentences.zh: 秋，崇韜將兵征蜀，以手書告憲曰：「允中避事久矣，餘受命西征，已奏還公黃閣。」

translations.literal: In autumn Chongtao was leading troops to campaign in Shu and wrote Xian by hand, "Yunzhong has long avoided affairs; I have received orders for the western campaign and have already memorialized to return you to the Yellow Pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Chongtao was leading troops to campaign in Shu and wrote Xian by hand, "Yunzhong has long avoided affairs; I have received orders for the western campaign and have already memorialized to return you to the Yellow Pavilion."

sentences.zh: 憲報曰：「庖人之代屍祝，所謂非吾事也。」

translations.literal: Xian replied, "For the cook to stand in for the invocator of the dead—this is what is called not my affair."
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "For the cook to stand in for the invocator of the dead—this is what is called not my affair."

sentences.zh: 時樞密承旨段徊當權任事，以憲從龍舊望，不欲憲在朝廷。

translations.literal: At that time Duan Huai, chief drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs, held power and managed affairs; because of Xian's old prestige as a follower of the dragon, he did not want Xian in the court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Duan Huai, chief drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs, held power and managed affairs; because of Xian's old prestige as a follower of the dragon, he did not want Xian at court.

sentences.zh: 會孟知祥鎮蜀川，選北京留守，徊揚言曰：「北門，國家根本，非重德不可輕授；

translations.literal: When Meng Zhixiang was posted to govern Shu, the northern capital intendant was to be chosen. Huai proclaimed publicly, "The northern gate is the root of the state; without great virtue it cannot be lightly conferred;
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zhixiang was posted to govern Shu, the northern capital intendant was to be chosen. Huai proclaimed publicly, "The northern gate is the root of the state; without great virtue it cannot be lightly conferred;

sentences.zh: 今之取才，非憲不可。」

translations.literal: for selecting talent today, none but Xian will do."
translations.idiomatic: for selecting talent today, none but Xian will do."

sentences.zh: 趨時者因附徊勢，巧中傷之。

translations.literal: Those who courted the times attached themselves to Huai's power and craftily slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who courted the times attached themselves to Huai's power and craftily slandered him.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「憲有相業，然國祚中興，宰相在天子麵前，得失可以改作；

translations.literal: He also said, "Xian has the makings of a chief minister, yet with the dynasty's fortunes reviving, a chancellor stands before the Son of Heaven and gains and losses can be revised;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Xian has the makings of a chief minister, yet with the dynasty's fortunes reviving, a chancellor stands before the Son of Heaven and gains and losses can be revised;

sentences.zh: 一方之事，製在一人，惟北面事重。」

translations.literal: affairs of a single region are controlled by one man, and only the northern frontier matter is weighty."
translations.idiomatic: affairs of a single region are controlled by one man, and only the northern frontier matter is weighty."

sentences.zh: 十一月，授憲銀青光祿大夫、檢校吏部尚書、太原尹、北京留守，知府事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Xian was appointed Silver Brightness Grand Master of the Palace, acting minister of personnel, prefect of Taiyuan, northern capital intendant, and given charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Xian was appointed Silver Brightness Grand Master of the Palace, acting minister of personnel, prefect of Taiyuan, northern capital intendant, and given charge of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，趙在禮入魏州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili entered Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili entered Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 時憲家屬在魏，關東俶擾，在禮善待其家，遣人齎書至太原誘憲。

translations.literal: At that time Xian's family were in Wei; the east of the Pass was suddenly in turmoil. Zaili treated his family well and sent a man bearing a letter to Taiyuan to entice Xian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xian's family were in Wei; the east of the Pass was suddenly in turmoil. Zaili treated his family well and sent a man bearing a letter to Taiyuan to entice Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲斬其使，書不發函而奏。

translations.literal: Xian beheaded the envoy, did not open the letter's seal, and memorialized about it.
translations.idiomatic: Xian beheaded the envoy, did not open the letter's seal, and memorialized about it.

sentences.zh: 既而明宗為兵眾所劫，諸軍離散，地遠不知事實，或謂憲曰：「蜀軍未至，洛陽窘急，總管又失兵權，製在諸軍之手，又聞河朔推戴，事若實然，或可濟否？」

translations.literal: Soon afterward Mingzong was seized by the troops, the armies scattered, and being far away they did not know the facts. Someone said to Xian, "The Shu army has not arrived; Luoyang is in dire straits; the chief commander has also lost military authority—control is in the hands of the armies. We also hear that Hebei is pushing for enthronement. If matters are indeed so, might it perhaps succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Mingzong was seized by the troops, the armies scattered, and being far away they did not know the facts. Someone said to Xian, "The Shu army has not arrived; Luoyang is in dire straits; the chief commander has also lost military authority—control is in the hands of the armies. We also hear that Hebei is pushing for enthronement. If matters are indeed so, might it perhaps succeed?"

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「治亂之機，間不容發，以愚所斷，事未可知。

translations.literal: Xian said, "The pivot of order and chaos admits no interval; as I judge it in my folly, the outcome is not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "The pivot of order and chaos admits no interval; as I judge it in my folly, the outcome is not yet known.

sentences.zh: 愚聞藥縱之言，總管德量仁厚，素得士心，餘勿多言，誌此而已。」

translations.literal: I have heard Yao Zongzhi's words: the chief commander's virtue and magnanimity are benevolent and generous, and he has long won the hearts of officers. Say no more—record only this."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard Yao Zongzhi's words: the chief commander's virtue and magnanimity are benevolent and generous, and he has long won the hearts of officers. Say no more—record only this."

sentences.zh: 四月五日，李存渥自洛陽至，口傳莊宗命，並無書詔，惟云天子授以隻箭，傳之為信。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fourth month Li Cunwo arrived from Luoyang, orally transmitting Zhuangzong's command without any written edict, saying only that the Son of Heaven had given him a single arrow and that passing it on was proof.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fourth month Li Cunwo arrived from Luoyang, orally transmitting Zhuangzong's command without any written edict, saying only that the Son of Heaven had given him a single arrow and that passing it on was proof.

sentences.zh: 眾心惑之，時事莫測。

translations.literal: The hearts of the crowd were perplexed; the times could not be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: The hearts of the crowd were perplexed; the times could not be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 左右獻畫曰：「存渥所乘馬，已戢其飾，復召人謀事，必行陰禍，因欲據城。

translations.literal: Those at his side offered a plan: "The horse Cunwo rides has already had its trappings removed; he has again summoned men to plot—he will surely carry out a hidden harm and thereby seize the city.
translations.idiomatic: Those at his side offered a plan: "The horse Cunwo rides has already had its trappings removed; he has again summoned men to plot—he will surely carry out a hidden harm and thereby seize the city.

sentences.zh: 寧我負人，宜早為之所，但戮呂、鄭二宦，且係存渥，徐觀其變，事萬全矣。」

translations.literal: Better that I wrong others than be wronged—act early. Only kill the two eunuchs Lü and Zheng, detain Cunwo for the time being, and watch developments slowly; then the affair will be entirely secure."
translations.idiomatic: Better that I wrong others than be wronged—act early. Only kill the two eunuchs Lü and Zheng, detain Cunwo for the time being, and watch developments slowly; then the affair will be entirely secure."

sentences.zh: 憲良久曰：「吾本書生，無軍功而致身及此，一旦自布衣而紆金紫，向來仕宦非出他門，此畫非吾心也。

translations.literal: Xian was silent a long while and said, "I was originally a scholar; without military achievement I have reached this position. In a single day I went from common cloth to gold and purple. My official career has never come through another gate—this plan is not in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was silent a long while and said, "I was originally a scholar; without military achievement I have reached this position. In a single day I went from common cloth to gold and purple. My official career has never come through another gate—this plan is not in my heart.

sentences.zh: 事苟不濟，以身徇義。」

translations.literal: If the affair does not succeed, I will give my body in loyalty to principle."
translations.idiomatic: If the affair does not succeed, I will give my body in loyalty to principle."

sentences.zh: 〈（《東都事略·張昭傳》：昭勸憲奉表明宗以勸進，憲曰：「吾書生也，天子委以保厘之任，吾豈苟生者乎！」

translations.literal: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Zhang Zhao: Zhao urged Xian to submit a memorial to Mingzong to urge his advance to the throne. Xian said, "I am a scholar. The Son of Heaven entrusted me with the charge of guarding and comforting the region—how could I cling to life!"
translations.idiomatic: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Zhang Zhao: Zhao urged Xian to submit a memorial to Mingzong to urge his advance to the throne. Xian said, "I am a scholar. The Son of Heaven entrusted me with the charge of guarding and comforting the region—how could I cling to life!"

sentences.zh: 昭曰：「此古之大節，公能行之，忠臣也。」

translations.literal: Zhao said, "This is the great integrity of antiquity. If you can act on it, you are a loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "This is the great integrity of antiquity. If you can act on it, you are a loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 憲既死，論者以昭能成憲之節。）〉

translations.literal: After Xian died, commentators held that Zhao had been able to bring Xian's integrity to completion.)〉
translations.idiomatic: After Xian died, commentators held that Zhao had been able to bring Xian's integrity to completion.)〉

sentences.zh: 翌日，符彥超誅呂、鄭，軍城大亂，燔剽達曙。

translations.literal: The next day Fu Yanchao executed Lü and Zheng; the military city fell into great disorder, and burning and plunder continued until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fu Yanchao executed Lü and Zheng; the military city fell into great disorder, and burning and plunder continued until dawn.

sentences.zh: 憲初聞有變，出奔沂州。

translations.literal: When Xian first heard of the disturbance he fled to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian first heard of the disturbance he fled to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 既而有司糾其委城之罪，四月二十四日，賜死於晉陽之千佛院。

translations.literal: Soon the authorities impeached him for the crime of abandoning the city. On the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month he was granted death at the Thousand Buddha Monastery in Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the authorities impeached him for the crime of abandoning the city. On the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month he was granted death at the Thousand Buddha Monastery in Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 幼子凝隨父走，亦為收者加害。

translations.literal: His young son Ning fled with his father and was also harmed by those who seized them.
translations.idiomatic: His young son Ning fled with his father and was also harmed by those who seized them.

sentences.zh: 明宗郊禮大赦，有司請昭雪，從之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong performed the suburban sacrifice and proclaimed a great amnesty, the authorities requested that Xian be cleared, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong performed the suburban sacrifice and proclaimed a great amnesty, the authorities requested that Xian be cleared, and it was granted.

sentences.zh: 憲沈靜寡欲，喜聚圖書，家書五千卷，視事之餘，手自刊校。

translations.literal: Xian was deep and calm, with few desires; he loved to collect books and had five thousand volumes in his family library. In the intervals of conducting affairs he personally collated and proofread them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was deep and calm, with few desires; he loved to collect books and had five thousand volumes in his family library. In the intervals of conducting affairs he personally collated and proofread them.

sentences.zh: 善彈琴，不飲酒，賓僚宴語，但論文嘯詠而已，士友重之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at the zither and did not drink wine; at banquets with guests and staff he discussed only literature and chanting poetry, and scholar-friends held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at the zither and did not drink wine; at banquets with guests and staff he discussed only literature and chanting poetry, and scholar-friends held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 憲長子守素，仕晉，位至尚書。

translations.literal: Xian's eldest son Shousu served Jin and rose to the rank of Secretariat director.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's eldest son Shousu served Jin and rose to the rank of Secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 王正言，鄆州人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhengyan was a man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengyan was a native of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父誌，濟陰令。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was magistrate of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi was magistrate of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 正言早孤貧，從沙門學，工詩，密州刺史賀德倫令歸俗，署郡職。

translations.literal: Zhengyan was orphaned early and poor; he studied under Buddhist monks and was skilled at poetry. The prefect of Mizhou, He Delun, had him return to lay life and appointed him to a prefectural post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan was orphaned early and poor; he studied under Buddhist monks and was skilled at poetry. The prefect of Mizhou, He Delun, had him return to lay life and appointed him to a prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 德倫鎮青州，表為推官；

translations.literal: When Delun was posted to Qingzhou he recommended him as investigating officer;
translations.idiomatic: When Delun was posted to Qingzhou he recommended him as investigating officer;

sentences.zh: 移鎮魏州，改觀察判官。

translations.literal: when he moved his command to Weizhou, he was made investigating officer for the surveillance commission.
translations.idiomatic: when he moved his command to Weizhou, he was made investigating officer for the surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平定魏博，正言仍舊職任，小心端慎，與物無競。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Weibo, Zhengyan remained in his former post, careful and upright, without striving against others.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong pacified Weibo, Zhengyan remained in his former post, careful and upright, without striving against others.

sentences.zh: 嘗為同職司空頲所淩，正言降心下之。

translations.literal: He was once bullied by his colleague Sikong Ting; Zhengyan lowered his heart and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was once bullied by his colleague Sikong Ting; Zhengyan humbled himself and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 頲誅，代為節度判官。

translations.literal: When Ting was executed, he replaced him as investigating officer for the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting was executed, he replaced him as investigating officer for the military commission.

sentences.zh: 同光初，守戶部尚書、興唐尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he held the posts of minister of revenue and prefect of Xingtang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tongguang he held the posts of minister of revenue and prefect of Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 時孔謙為租庸副使，常畏張憲挺特，不欲其領使，乃白郭崇韜留憲於魏州，請宰相豆盧革判租庸。

translations.literal: At that time Kong Qian was deputy commissioner of transport and corvée tax; he often feared Zhang Xian's uprightness and did not want him to head the commission, so he told Guo Chongtao to keep Xian at Weizhou and asked the chancellor Dou Luge to take charge of transport and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kong Qian was deputy commissioner of transport and corvée tax; he often feared Zhang Xian's uprightness and did not want him to head the commission, so he told Guo Chongtao to keep Xian at Weizhou and asked the chancellor Dou Luge to take charge of transport and corvée.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復以盧質代之。

translations.literal: Before long Lu Zhi was again made to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lu Zhi was again made to replace him.

sentences.zh: 孔謙白云：「錢穀重務，宰相事多，簿籍留滯。」

translations.literal: Kong Qian reported, "Revenue and grain are weighty affairs; the chancellor has many duties and the ledgers are delayed."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian reported, "Revenue and grain are weighty affairs; the chancellor has many duties and the ledgers are delayed."

sentences.zh: 又云：「盧質判二日，便借官錢，皆不可任。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Within two days of Lu Zhi taking charge he borrowed official funds—none of them can be entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Within two days of Lu Zhi taking charge he borrowed official funds—none of them can be entrusted."

sentences.zh: 意謂崇韜必令己代其任，時物議未允而止，謙沮喪久之。

translations.literal: He meant that Chongtao would surely have him replace the post, but public opinion at the time did not approve and it stopped; Qian was dejected for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He meant that Chongtao would surely have him replace the post, but public opinion at the time did not approve and it stopped; Qian was dejected for a long time.

sentences.zh: 李紹宏曰：「邦計國本，時號怨府，非張憲不稱職。」

translations.literal: Li Shaohong said, "State revenue is the root of the realm; it is called the office of complaints—none but Zhang Xian is fit for the post."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaohong said, "State revenue is the root of the realm; it is called the office of complaints—none but Zhang Xian is fit for the post."

sentences.zh: 即日征之。

translations.literal: That very day he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he was summoned.

sentences.zh: 孔謙、段徊白崇韜曰：「邦計雖重，在侍中眼前，但得一人為使即可。

translations.literal: Kong Qian and Duan Huai told Chongtao, "State revenue is weighty, but it is before the Vice Director's eyes—one man as commissioner will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian and Duan Huai told Chongtao, "State revenue is weighty, but it is before the Vice Director's eyes—one man as commissioner will suffice.

sentences.zh: 魏博六州戶口，天下之半，王正言操守有餘，智力不足，若朝廷任使，庶幾與人共事；

translations.literal: The six prefectures of Weibo account for half the empire's households. Wang Zhengyan has integrity to spare but insufficient intelligence; if the court appoints him, he might perhaps work with others;
translations.idiomatic: The six prefectures of Weibo account for half the empire's households. Wang Zhengyan has integrity to spare but insufficient intelligence; if the court appoints him, he might perhaps work with others;

sentences.zh: 若專製方隅，未見其可。

translations.literal: if he were given sole control of a region, his fitness is not yet seen.
translations.idiomatic: if he were given sole control of a region, his fitness is not yet seen.

sentences.zh: 張憲才器兼濟，宜以委之。」

translations.literal: Zhang Xian's talent and capacity are comprehensive—he should be entrusted with it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian's talent and capacity are comprehensive—he should be entrusted with it."

sentences.zh: 崇韜即奏憲留守魏州，征王正言為租庸使。

translations.literal: Chongtao immediately memorialized that Xian remain intendant at Weizhou and summoned Wang Zhengyan as commissioner of transport and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao immediately memorialized that Xian remain intendant at Weizhou and summoned Wang Zhengyan as commissioner of transport and corvée.

sentences.zh: 正言在職，主諾而已，權柄出於孔謙。

translations.literal: In office Zhengyan merely assented; real authority lay with Kong Qian.
translations.idiomatic: In office Zhengyan merely assented; real authority lay with Kong Qian.

sentences.zh: 正言不耐繁浩，簿領縱橫，觸事遺忘，物論以為不可，即以孔謙代之，正言守禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Zhengyan could not bear the complexity; ledgers crisscrossed and he forgot matters at every turn. Public opinion held this unacceptable, so Kong Qian replaced him and Zhengyan remained minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan could not bear the complexity; ledgers crisscrossed and he forgot matters at every turn. Public opinion held this unacceptable, so Kong Qian replaced him and Zhengyan remained minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，代張憲為興唐尹，留守鄴都。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he replaced Zhang Xian as prefect of Xingtang and remained intendant at Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he replaced Zhang Xian as prefect of Xingtang and remained intendant at Yedu.

sentences.zh: 時武德使史彥瓊，監守鄴都，廩帑出納，兵馬製置，皆出彥瓊，將佐官吏，頤指氣使，正言不能以道禦之，但趑趄聽命。

translations.literal: At that time the Military Virtue commissioner Shi Yanqiong supervised and guarded Yedu; granary receipts and disbursements and military arrangements all issued from Yanqiong. Generals, staff, and officials he ordered about imperiously; Zhengyan could not restrain him by principle but only hesitated and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Military Virtue commissioner Shi Yanqiong supervised and guarded Yedu; granary receipts and disbursements and military arrangements all issued from Yanqiong. Generals, staff, and officials he ordered about imperiously; Zhengyan could not restrain him by principle but only hesitated and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 至是，貝州戍兵亂，入魏州，彥瓊望風敗走，亂兵剽劫坊市。

translations.literal: At this time the garrison troops of Beizhou mutinied and entered Weizhou; Yanqiong fled at the mere rumor of their approach, and the mutineers plundered the wards and markets.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the garrison troops of Beizhou mutinied and entered Weizhou; Yanqiong fled at the mere rumor of their approach, and the mutineers plundered the wards and markets.

sentences.zh: 正言促召書吏寫奏章，家人曰：「賊已殺人縱火，都城已陷，何奏之有。」

translations.literal: Zhengyan urgently summoned clerks to draft a memorial; his family said, "The rebels have already killed and set fires—the capital has fallen; what memorial is there to write?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan urgently summoned clerks to draft a memorial; his family said, "The rebels have already killed and set fires—the capital has fallen; what memorial is there to write?"

sentences.zh: 是日，正言引諸僚佐謁趙在禮，

translations.literal: That day Zhengyan led his staff to call on Zhao Zaili,
translations.idiomatic: That day Zhengyan led his staff to call on Zhao Zaili,

sentences.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：正言索馬，不能得，乃帥僚佐步出府門謁在禮。）〉

translations.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Zhengyan sought a horse but could not obtain one, so he led his staff on foot out the prefectural gate to call on Zaili.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Comprehensive Mirror: Zhengyan sought a horse but could not obtain one, so he led his staff on foot out the prefectural gate to call on Zaili.)〉

sentences.zh: 望塵再拜請罪。

translations.literal: Bowing twice in the dust to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Bowing twice in the dust to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 在禮曰：「尚書重德，勿自卑屈，餘受國恩，與尚書共事，但思歸之眾，倉卒見迫耳。」

translations.literal: Zaili said, "Minister, your virtue is weighty—do not humble yourself. I have received the state's grace and work with the Minister, but the crowd longs to return home and was pressed in haste."
translations.idiomatic: Zaili said, "Minister, your virtue is weighty—do not humble yourself. I have received the state's grace and work with the Minister, but the crowd longs to return home and was pressed in haste."

sentences.zh: 因拜正言，厚加慰撫。

translations.literal: He then bowed to Zhengyan and comforted him generously.
translations.idiomatic: He then bowed to Zhengyan and comforted him generously.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，正言求為平盧軍行軍司馬，因以授之，竟卒於任。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Zhengyan requested to be acting commander of the Pinglu army and was accordingly appointed; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Zhengyan asked to serve as acting commander of the Pinglu army and received the post; he died in that office.

sentences.zh: 胡裝，禮部尚書曾之孫。

translations.literal: Hu Zhuang was the grandson of Zeng, minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhuang was the grandson of Zeng, minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 汴將楊師厚之鎮魏州，裝與副使李嗣業有舊，因往依之，薦授貴鄉令。

translations.literal: When the Bian general Yang Shihou was posted to Weizhou, Zhuang had old ties with the deputy commissioner Li Siye and went to rely on him; he was recommended and appointed magistrate of Guixiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bian general Yang Shihou was posted to Weizhou, Zhuang had old ties with the deputy commissioner Li Siye and went to rely on him; he was recommended and appointed magistrate of Guixiang.

sentences.zh: 及張彥之亂，嗣業遇害，裝罷秩，客於魏州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yan's rebellion broke out, Siye met with disaster; Zhuang lost his post and lived as a guest in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yan's rebellion broke out, Siye was killed; Zhuang lost his post and lived as a guest in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初至，裝謁見，求假官，司空頲以其居官貪濁，不得調者久之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong first arrived, Zhuang called on him and sought a provisional appointment; Sikong Ting, because Zhuang had been corrupt in office, long kept him from receiving a transfer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first arrived, Zhuang called on him and sought a provisional appointment; Sikong Ting, because Zhuang had been corrupt in office, long kept him from receiving a transfer.

sentences.zh: 十三年，莊宗還太原，裝候於離亭；

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan; Zhuang waited at the parting pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan; Zhuang waited at the parting pavilion;

sentences.zh: 謁者不內，乃排闥而入，曰：「臣本朝公卿子孫，從兵至此。

translations.literal: the usher would not admit him, so he forced the door and entered, saying, "Your servant is a descendant of this dynasty's dukes and ministers and has followed the army to this place.
translations.idiomatic: the usher would not admit him, so he forced the door and entered, saying, "I am a descendant of this dynasty's dukes and ministers and have followed the army to this place.

sentences.zh: 殿下比襲唐祚，勤求英俊，以壯霸圖。

translations.literal: Your Highness has lately assumed the Tang succession and diligently seeks outstanding men to strengthen the hegemonic design.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has lately assumed the Tang succession and diligently seeks outstanding men to strengthen your hegemonic design.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不才，比於進九九，納豎刁、頭須，亦所庶幾。

translations.literal: Though your servant lacks talent, compared with advancing Jiu Jiu or welcoming Shu Diao and Tou Xu, he is not far from their measure.
translations.idiomatic: Though I lack talent, I am scarcely inferior to those who advanced Jiu Jiu or welcomed Shu Diao and Tou Xu to court.

sentences.zh: 而羈旅累年，執事者不垂顧錄，臣不能赴海觸樹，走胡適越，今日歸死於殿下也！」

translations.literal: Yet for years in exile those in charge have not extended regard or enrollment. Your servant cannot throw himself into the sea or dash against a tree, nor flee to Hu or Yue—today he returns to die before Your Highness!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet for years in exile those in charge have not extended their regard. I cannot throw myself into the sea or dash against a tree, nor flee to Hu or Yue—today I return to die before Your Highness!"

sentences.zh: 莊宗愕然曰：「孤未之知，何至如是！」

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said in astonishment, "I did not know of this—how could it come to such a pass!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said in astonishment, "I did not know of this—how could it come to such a pass!"

sentences.zh: 賜酒食慰遣之，謂郭崇韜曰：「便與擬議。」

translations.literal: He bestowed wine and food to comfort and dismiss him, and told Guo Chongtao, "Draw up a proposal at once."
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed wine and food to comfort and dismiss him, and told Guo Chongtao, "Draw up a proposal at once."

sentences.zh: 是歲，署館驛巡官。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed touring officer of the post stations.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed touring officer of the post stations.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授監察御史裏行，遷節度巡官，賜緋魚袋；

translations.literal: Before long he was made acting surveillance censor, promoted to touring officer of the military commission, and granted scarlet robes and the fish bag;
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting surveillance censor, promoted to touring officer of the military commission, and granted scarlet robes and the fish bag;

sentences.zh: 尋曆推官、檢校員外郎。

translations.literal: soon he served in succession as investigating officer and acting director in a bureau.
translations.idiomatic: soon he served in succession as investigating officer and acting director in a bureau.

sentences.zh: 裝學書無師法，工詩非作者，僻於題壁，所至宮亭寺觀，必書爵裏，人或譏之，不以為愧。

translations.literal: Zhuang studied calligraphy without proper method and wrote poetry without being a true author; he was fond of inscribing walls, and wherever he went among palaces, pavilions, temples, and shrines he always wrote his rank and residence—people sometimes mocked him, but he felt no shame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang studied calligraphy without proper training and wrote poetry without being a true poet; he was fond of inscribing walls, and wherever he went among palaces, pavilions, temples, and shrines he always wrote his rank and residence—people sometimes mocked him, but he felt no shame.

sentences.zh: 時四鎮幕賓皆金紫，裝獨恥銀艾。

translations.literal: At that time staff guests of the four commands all wore gold and purple; Zhuang alone was ashamed of silver and green.
translations.idiomatic: At that time staff guests of the four commands all wore gold and purple; Zhuang alone was ashamed of silver and green.

sentences.zh: 十七年，莊宗自魏州之德勝，與賓僚城樓餞別，既而群僚離席，裝獨留，獻詩三篇，意在章服。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Zhuangzong went from Weizhou to Desheng; on the city tower he gave a farewell feast for his guests and staff. When the group had left their seats Zhuang alone remained and presented three poems, his aim being official robes and insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Zhuangzong went from Weizhou to Desheng; on the city tower he gave a farewell feast for his guests and staff. When the group had left their seats Zhuang alone remained and presented three poems, his aim being official robes and insignia.

sentences.zh: 莊宗舉大鍾屬裝曰：「員外能釂此乎？」

translations.literal: Zhuangzong raised a great bell-cup and handed it to Zhuang, saying, "Director, can you drain this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong raised a great bell-cup and handed it to Zhuang, saying, "Director, can you drain this?"

sentences.zh: 裝飲酒素少，略無難色，為之一舉而釂，莊宗即解紫袍賜之。

translations.literal: Zhuang ordinarily drank little but showed hardly any difficulty and drained it in one draft; Zhuangzong at once removed his purple robe and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang ordinarily drank little but showed hardly any difficulty and drained it in one draft; Zhuangzong at once removed his purple robe and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 同光初，以裝為給事中，從幸洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was made attendant in the Secretariat and followed the emperor to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tongguang he was made attendant in the Secretariat and followed the emperor to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時連年大水，百官多窘，裝求為襄州副使。

translations.literal: At that time floods came year after year and many officials were in straits; Zhuang sought to be deputy commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time floods came year after year and many officials were in straits; Zhuang sought to be deputy commissioner of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，洛陽變擾，節度使劉訓以私忿族裝，誣奏雲裝欲謀亂，人士冤之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Luoyang was thrown into turmoil; the military commissioner Liu Xun, from private resentment, exterminated Zhuang's clan and falsely memorialized that Zhuang intended rebellion; men of standing held it a grievous injustice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Luoyang was thrown into turmoil; the military commissioner Liu Xun, from private resentment, exterminated Zhuang's clan and falsely memorialized that Zhuang intended rebellion; men of standing held it a grievous injustice.

sentences.zh: 崔貽孫，

translations.literal: Cui Yisun,
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yisun,

sentences.zh: 〈（《新唐書·宰相世係表》：貽孫字伯垂。）〉

translations.literal: (New Book of Tang, Genealogical Tables of Chief Ministers: Yisun's style was Bochui.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (New Book of Tang, Genealogical Tables of Chief Ministers: Yisun's style was Bochui.)〉

sentences.zh: 祖元亮，左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuanliang was Left Regular Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuanliang was Left Regular Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 〈（《世係表》：元亮，字晦孫，虢州刺史。）〉

translations.literal: (Genealogical Tables: Yuanliang, styled Huisun, was prefect of Guo.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Genealogical Tables: Yuanliang, styled Huisun, was prefect of Guo.)〉

sentences.zh: 父芻言，潞州判官。

translations.literal: His father Chuyan was judge of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chuyan was judge of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 貽孫以門族登進士第，以監察升朝，曆清資美職。

translations.literal: Yisun, through his clan standing, passed the jinshi examination, rose to court through surveillance censor, and held in succession pure and eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun, through his clan standing, passed the jinshi examination, rose to court through surveillance censor, and held in succession pure and eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 及為省郎，使於江南回，以橐裝營別墅於漢上之穀城，退居自奉。

translations.literal: When he became a Secretariat director and returned from a mission to Jiangnan, he used his traveling funds to build a villa at Gucheng on the Han and retired to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he became a Secretariat director and returned from a mission to Jiangnan, he used his traveling funds to build a villa at Gucheng on the Han and retired to support himself.

sentences.zh: 清江之上，綠竹遍野，狹徑濃密，維舟曲岸，人莫造焉，時人甚高之。

translations.literal: On the clear river green bamboo spread over the fields; narrow paths lay thick and dense; he moored his boat on a winding bank where no one could approach—men of the time held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: On the clear river green bamboo spread over the fields; narrow paths lay thick and dense; he moored his boat on a winding bank where no one could approach—men of the time held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 及李振貶均州，貽孫曲奉之。

translations.literal: When Li Zhen was demoted to Junzhou, Yisun curried favor with him obsequiously.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhen was demoted to Junzhou, Yisun curried favor with him obsequiously.

sentences.zh: 振入朝，貽孫累遷丞郎。

translations.literal: When Zhen entered court, Yisun was repeatedly promoted to director posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen entered court, Yisun was repeatedly promoted to director posts.

sentences.zh: 同光初，除吏部侍郎，銓選疏謬，貶官塞地，馳驛至潞州，致書於府帥孔曰：「十五年穀城山裏，自謂逸人；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was made vice minister of personnel; his civil-service selection was careless and mistaken, and he was demoted to a frontier post. He rode post-horses to Luzhou and sent a letter to the prefect Kong Qing, saying, "For fifteen years in the Gucheng mountains I called myself a recluse;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tongguang he was made vice minister of personnel; his civil-service selection was careless and mistaken, and he was demoted to a frontier post. He rode post-horses to Luzhou and sent a letter to the prefect Kong Qing, saying, "For fifteen years in the Gucheng mountains I called myself a recluse;

sentences.zh: 二千里沙塞途中，今為逐客。」

translations.literal: on a two-thousand-li road through sand and border passes I am now an exile."
translations.idiomatic: on a two-thousand-li road through sand and border passes I am now an exile."

sentences.zh: 以其年八十，奏留府下。

translations.literal: Because he was eighty years old, it was memorialized that he remain under the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was eighty years old, it was memorialized that he remain under the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，量移澤州司馬，遇赦還京。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred in measure to military adjutant of Zezhou; on encountering an amnesty he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred in measure to military adjutant of Zezhou; on encountering an amnesty he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭玨以姻戚之分，復擬吏部侍郎，天官任重，昏耄罔知，後遷禮部尚書，致仕而卒。

translations.literal: The chancellor Zheng Jue, through ties of marriage kin, again proposed him as vice minister of personnel. The Ministry of Personnel bears heavy responsibility, yet in senility he knew nothing; later he was transferred to minister of rites, retired from office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor Zheng Jue, through ties of marriage kin, again proposed him as vice minister of personnel. The Ministry of Personnel bears heavy responsibility, yet in senility he knew nothing; later he was transferred to minister of rites, retired from office, and died.

sentences.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：崔貽孫年過八十，求進不休，囊橐之資，素有貯積，性好幹人，喜得小惠。）〉

translations.literal: (Northern Dreams Miscellany: Cui Yisun passed eighty yet never ceased seeking advancement; he had long stored funds in purse and bag; by nature he loved to meddle in others' affairs and delighted in small favors.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Northern Dreams Miscellany: Cui Yisun passed eighty yet never ceased seeking advancement; he had long stored funds in purse and bag; by nature he loved to meddle in others' affairs and delighted in small favors.)〉

sentences.zh: 有子三人，自貽孫左降之後，各於舊業爭分其利，甘旨醫藥，莫有奉者。

translations.literal: He had three sons; after Yisun's demotion each contended for a share of the profit from his former holdings—delicacies and medicine, none provided.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons; after Yisun's demotion each contended for a share of the profit from his former holdings—delicacies and medicine, none provided.

sentences.zh: 貽孫以書責之云：「生有明君宰相，死有天曹地府，吾雖考終，豈放汝耶！」

translations.literal: Yisun wrote to reprove them, saying, "In life there are enlightened rulers and chancellors; in death there are the celestial and earthly courts—though I die in my bed, how could I let you go!"
translations.idiomatic: Yisun wrote to reprove them, saying, "In life there are enlightened rulers and chancellors; in death there are the celestial and earthly courts—though I die in my bed, how could I let you go!"

sentences.zh: 孟鵠，魏州人。

translations.literal: Meng Hu was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hu was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初定魏博，選幹吏以計兵賦，以鵠為度支孔目官。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong first pacified Weibo he selected capable officials to calculate military levies and made Hu a clerical officer in the expenditure section.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first pacified Weibo he selected capable officials to calculate military levies and made Hu a clerical officer in the expenditure section.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，為邢洺節度使，每曲意承迎，明宗甚德之。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong he was military commissioner of Xing and Mo; he always curried favor obsequiously, and Mingzong was deeply grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he was military commissioner of Xing and Mo; he always curried favor obsequiously, and Mingzong was deeply grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 及孔謙專典軍賦，徵督苛急，明宗嘗切齒。

translations.literal: When Kong Qian monopolized military supplies and collection and requisition were harsh and urgent, Mingzong once gnashed his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Qian monopolized military supplies and collection and requisition were harsh and urgent, Mingzong once gnashed his teeth.

sentences.zh: 及即位，鵠自租庸勾官擢為客省副使、樞密承旨，遷三司副使，出為相州刺史。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Hu was promoted from transport-and-corvée checking officer to deputy commissioner of the guest bureau and chief drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then transferred to deputy commissioner of the three departments and sent out as prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, Hu was promoted from transport-and-corvée checking officer to deputy commissioner of the guest bureau and chief drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then transferred to deputy commissioner of the three departments and sent out as prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會範延光再遷樞密，乃征鵠為三司使。

translations.literal: When Fan Yanguang was again transferred to the Bureau of Military Affairs, Hu was summoned as commissioner of the three departments.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang was again transferred to the Bureau of Military Affairs, Hu was summoned as commissioner of the three departments.

sentences.zh: 初，鵠有計畫之能，及專掌邦賦，操割依違，名譽頓減。

translations.literal: At first Hu had the ability to plan; once he monopolized state revenue he manipulated and extorted inconsistently, and his reputation suddenly declined.
translations.idiomatic: At first Hu had the ability to plan; once he monopolized state revenue he manipulated and extorted inconsistently, and his reputation suddenly declined.

sentences.zh: 期年發疾，求外任，仍授許州節度使。

translations.literal: Within a year he fell ill, sought an outer appointment, and was still made military commissioner of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he fell ill, sought an outer appointment, and was still made military commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 謝恩退，帝目送之，顧為侍臣曰：「孟鵠掌三司幾年，得至方鎮？」

translations.literal: After thanking the emperor for grace and withdrawing, the emperor watched him go with his eyes and turned to the attending ministers, saying, "Meng Hu headed the three departments for how many years that he could reach a frontier command?"
translations.idiomatic: After thanking the emperor for grace and withdrawing, the emperor watched him go with his eyes and turned to the attending ministers, saying, "Meng Hu headed the three departments for how many years that he could reach a frontier command?"

sentences.zh: 範延光奏曰：「鵠於同光世已為三司勾官，天成初為三司副使，出刺相州，入判三司又二年。」

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang memorialized, "In the Tongguang era Hu was already a checking officer of the three departments; at the beginning of Tiancheng he was deputy commissioner, went out as prefect of Xiangzhou, and upon returning to judge the three departments served another two years."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang memorialized, "In the Tongguang era Hu was already a checking officer of the three departments; at the beginning of Tiancheng he was deputy commissioner, went out as prefect of Xiangzhou, and upon returning to judge the three departments served another two years."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「鵠以幹事，遽至方鎮，爭不勉旃。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Hu, through capable service, suddenly reached a frontier command—how could he not strive harder?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Hu, through capable service, suddenly reached a frontier command—how could he not strive harder?"

sentences.zh: 鵠與延光俱魏人，厚相結托，暨延光掌樞務，援引判三司，又致節鉞，明宗知之，故以此言譏之。

translations.literal: Hu and Yanguang were both men of Wei and bound themselves closely in mutual support; when Yanguang took charge of military affairs he recommended Hu to judge the three departments and also secured him a military commission. Mingzong knew this, and therefore spoke these words in sarcasm.
translations.idiomatic: Hu and Yanguang were both men of Wei and bound themselves closely in mutual support; when Yanguang took charge of military affairs he recommended Hu to judge the three departments and also secured him a military commission. Mingzong knew this, and therefore spoke these words in sarcasm.

sentences.zh: 到任未周歲，卒。

translations.literal: He had not completed a year in office when he died.
translations.idiomatic: He had not completed a year in office when he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 孫嶽，冀州人也。

translations.literal: Sun Yue was a man of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yue was a native of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 強幹有才用，曆府衛右職。

translations.literal: Forceful and capable, with talent and usefulness, he held in succession posts in the palace guards on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Forceful and capable, with talent and usefulness, he held in succession posts in the palace guards on the right.

sentences.zh: 天成中，為潁耀二州刺史、閬州團練使，所至稱治，遷鳳州節度使。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng he was prefect of Ying and Yao, defense commissioner of Langzhou; wherever he went he was praised for good governance, and he was transferred to military commissioner of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he was prefect of Ying and Yao, defense commissioner of Langzhou; wherever he went he was praised for good governance, and he was transferred to military commissioner of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 受代歸京，秦王從榮欲以嶽為元帥府都押衙，事未行，馮贇舉為三司使，時預密謀。

translations.literal: When relieved and returned to the capital, the Prince of Qin, Congrong, wished to make Yue chief military adjutant of the prince's headquarters; the matter had not been carried out when Feng Yun recommended him as commissioner of the three departments—at the time he shared in secret plotting.
translations.idiomatic: When relieved and returned to the capital, the Prince of Qin, Congrong, wished to make Yue chief military adjutant of the prince's headquarters; the matter had not been carried out when Feng Yun recommended him as commissioner of the three departments—at the time he shared in secret plotting.

sentences.zh: 朱、馮患從榮之恣橫，嶽曾極言其禍之端，康義誠聞之不悅。

translations.literal: Zhu and Feng feared Congrong's wanton arrogance; Yue had once spoken to the utmost of the beginnings of disaster, and Kang Yicheng heard it with displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu and Feng feared Congrong's wanton arrogance; Yue had once spoken to the utmost of the beginnings of disaster, and Kang Yicheng heard it with displeasure.

sentences.zh: 及從榮敗，義誠召嶽同至河南府檢閱府藏。

translations.literal: When Congrong was defeated, Yicheng summoned Yue to go with him to the Henan prefecture to inspect the prefectural treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Congrong was defeated, Yicheng summoned Yue to go with him to the Henan prefecture to inspect the prefectural treasury.

sentences.zh: 時紛擾未定，義誠密遣騎士射之，嶽走至通利坊，為騎士所害，識與不識皆痛之。

translations.literal: The turmoil was not yet settled; Yicheng secretly sent horsemen to shoot him. Yue fled to Tongli Ward and was killed by the horsemen; those who knew him and those who did not alike grieved.
translations.idiomatic: The turmoil was not yet settled; Yicheng secretly sent horsemen to shoot him. Yue fled to Tongli Ward and was killed by the horsemen; those who knew him and those who did not alike grieved.

sentences.zh: 子璉，曆諸衛將軍、藩閫節度副使。

translations.literal: His son Lian held in succession generalships in the guards and was deputy military commissioner of a frontier circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lian held in succession generalships in the guards and was deputy military commissioner of a frontier circuit.

sentences.zh: 張延朗，汴州開封人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanlang was a man of Kaifeng in Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanlang was a native of Kaifeng in Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 事梁，以租庸吏為鄆州糧料使。

translations.literal: He served Liang and, as a transport-and-corvée clerk, was grain supply officer of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang and, as a transport-and-corvée clerk, was grain supply officer of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 明宗克鄆州，得延朗，復以為糧料使，後徙鎮宣武、成德，以為元從孔目官。

translations.literal: When Mingzong captured Yanzhou he obtained Yanlang and again made him grain supply officer; later, when he moved his command to Xuanwu and Chengde, he made him a clerical officer among his original followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong captured Yanzhou he obtained Yanlang and again made him grain supply officer; later, when he moved his command to Xuanwu and Chengde, he made him a clerical officer among his original followers.

sentences.zh: 長興元年，始置三司使，拜延朗特進、工部尚書，充諸道鹽鐵轉運等使，兼判戶部度支事，詔以延朗充三司使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing the post of commissioner of the three departments was first established; Yanlang was appointed Special Advancement and minister of works, made commissioner of salt, iron, and transport for all circuits, and given concurrent charge of expenditure in the Ministry of Revenue; an edict appointed Yanlang commissioner of the three departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changxing the post of commissioner of the three departments was first established; Yanlang was appointed Special Advancement and minister of works, made commissioner of salt, iron, and transport for all circuits, and given concurrent charge of expenditure in the Ministry of Revenue; an edict appointed Yanlang commissioner of the three departments.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，授禮部尚書，兼中書侍郎、平章事、判三司。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne he was made minister of rites, concurrently vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and judge of the three departments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor took the throne he was made minister of rites, concurrently vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and judge of the three departments.

sentences.zh: 延朗再上表辭曰：

translations.literal: Yanlang again submitted a memorial declining, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang again submitted a memorial declining, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣濫承雨露，擢處鈞衡，兼叨選部之銜，仍掌計司之重。

translations.literal: Your servant has undeservedly received imperial grace, been raised to the balance of state, and undeservedly bears the title of the selection ministry while still holding the weight of the accounting office.
translations.idiomatic: I have undeservedly received imperial grace, been raised to the balance of state, and undeservedly bear the title of the selection ministry while still holding the weight of the accounting office.

sentences.zh: 況中省文章之地，洪爐陶鑄之門，臣自揣量，何以當處。

translations.literal: Moreover, the central secretariat is a place of literary composition, a great furnace and casting gate—your servant measures himself: how could he be fit for the post?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the central secretariat is a place of literary composition, a great furnace and casting gate—I measure myself: how could I be fit for the post?

sentences.zh: 是以繼陳章表，疊貢情誠，乞請睿恩，免貽朝論。

translations.literal: Therefore I have repeatedly submitted memorials and repeatedly offered sincere feeling, begging sagacious grace so as not to bring reproach upon court discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have repeatedly submitted memorials and repeatedly offered my sincere feeling, begging sagacious grace so as not to bring reproach upon court discussion.

sentences.zh: 豈謂禦批累降，聖旨不移，決以此官，委臣非器，所以強收涕泗，勉遏怔忪，重思事上之門，細料盡忠之路。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that imperial rescripts would descend again and again and the sacred decree would not shift, firmly fixing this office upon your servant, an unfit vessel? Therefore I force back tears, strive to restrain bewilderment, think again of the gate of serving superiors, and carefully plan the path of utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that imperial rescripts would descend again and again and the sacred decree would not shift, firmly fixing this office upon me, an unfit vessel? Therefore I force back tears, strive to restrain bewilderment, think again of the gate of serving superiors, and carefully plan the path of utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 竊以位高則危至，寵極則謗生，君臣莫保於初終，分義難防於毀譽。

translations.literal: I venture to hold that when position is high, peril arrives; when favor reaches its peak, slander arises—lord and minister cannot be preserved from beginning to end, and duty and righteousness are hard to guard against ruin and praise.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to hold that when position is high, peril arrives; when favor reaches its peak, slander arises—lord and minister cannot be preserved from beginning to end, and duty and righteousness are hard to guard against ruin and praise.

sentences.zh: 臣若保茲重任，忘彼至公，徇情而以免是非，偷安而以固富貴，則內欺心腑，外負聖朝，何以報君父之大恩，望子孫之延慶。

translations.literal: If your servant preserves this heavy responsibility yet forgets supreme fairness, indulges feeling to escape right and wrong, or seeks ease to secure wealth and rank, then inwardly he deceives his heart and outwardly he fails the sacred court—how could he repay the great grace of lord and father or hope for extended blessing for his sons and grandsons?
translations.idiomatic: If I preserve this heavy responsibility yet forget supreme fairness, indulge feeling to escape right and wrong, or seek ease to secure wealth and rank, then inwardly I deceive my heart and outwardly I fail the sacred court—how could I repay the great grace of lord and father or hope for extended blessing for my sons and grandsons?

sentences.zh: 臣若但行王道，惟守國章，任人必取當才，決事須依正理，確違形勢，堅塞幸門，則可以振舉宏綱，彌縫大化，助陛下含容之澤，彰國家至理之風，然而讒邪者必起憾詞，憎嫉者寧無謗議，或慮至尊未悉，群謗難明，不更拔本尋源，便俟甘瑕受玷，臣心可忍，臣恥可消。

translations.literal: If your servant only practices the kingly way and solely upholds the state's statutes, in appointing men always selects the fitting talent and in deciding affairs must rely on correct principle, firmly rejecting opportunism and stoutly blocking the gate of favor, then he can raise the great framework and mend the great transformation, assist Your Majesty's tolerant grace, and display the state's utmost principle—yet slanderers and the wicked will surely raise words of resentment, and the envious will scarcely be without calumny. Perhaps the utmost sovereign will not fully understand and the crowd of slanders will be hard to clarify; without pulling up the root and tracing the source, one would simply await willingness to accept a stain—your servant's heart could bear it, but his shame could not be erased.
translations.idiomatic: If I only practice the kingly way and solely uphold the state's statutes, in appointing men always select the fitting talent and in deciding affairs rely on correct principle, firmly rejecting opportunism and stoutly blocking the gate of favor, then I can raise the great framework and mend the great transformation, assist Your Majesty's tolerant grace, and display the state's utmost principle—yet slanderers and the wicked will surely raise words of resentment, and the envious will scarcely be without calumny. Perhaps the utmost sovereign will not fully understand and the crowd of slanders will be hard to clarify; without pulling up the root and tracing the source, one would simply await willingness to accept a stain—my heart could bear it, but my shame could not be erased.

sentences.zh: 隻恐山林草澤之人，稱量聖製；

translations.literal: I only fear that men of mountains, forests, grasslands, and marshes will weigh the sacred system;
translations.idiomatic: I only fear that men of mountains, forests, grasslands, and marshes will weigh the sacred system;

sentences.zh: 冠履軒裳之士，輕慢朝廷。

translations.literal: and gentlemen of caps, shoes, carriages, and robes will treat the court with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: and gentlemen of caps, shoes, carriages, and robes will treat the court with contempt.

sentences.zh: 臣又以國計一司，掌其經費，利權二務，職在捃收。

translations.literal: Your servant further considers that the state accounts office alone controls its expenditures; profit and authority are twin tasks whose duty lies in gathering revenue.
translations.idiomatic: I further consider that the state accounts office alone controls its expenditures; profit and authority are twin tasks whose duty lies in gathering revenue.

sentences.zh: 將欲養四海之貧民，無過薄賦；

translations.literal: If one wishes to support the poor people within the four seas, nothing surpasses light levies;
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes to support the poor people within the four seas, nothing surpasses light levies;

sentences.zh: 贍六軍之勁士，又藉豐儲。

translations.literal: to supply the stalwart soldiers of the six armies again depends on abundant stores.
translations.idiomatic: to supply the stalwart soldiers of the six armies again depends on abundant stores.

sentences.zh: 利害相隨，取與難酌，若使罄山采木，竭澤求魚，則地官之教化不行，國本之傷殘益甚，取怨黔首，是黷皇風。

translations.literal: Benefit and harm follow each other; taking and giving are hard to balance. If one exhausts the mountains to gather timber and drains the marshes to seek fish, then the Minister of Earth's instruction will not be carried out, injury to the state's root will grow worse, resentment will be taken from the black-haired people, and the imperial wind will be profaned.
translations.idiomatic: Benefit and harm follow each other; taking and giving are hard to balance. If one exhausts the mountains to gather timber and drains the marshes to seek fish, then the Minister of Earth's instruction will not be carried out, injury to the state's root will grow worse, resentment will be taken from the black-haired people, and the imperial wind will be profaned.

sentences.zh: 況諸道所征賦租，雖多數額，時逢水旱，或遇蟲霜，其間則有減無添，所在又申逃係欠。

translations.literal: Moreover, the land tax and rent levied by the various circuits, though nominally large in quota, often meet flood or drought or encounter insects and frost; among them there is reduction without increase, and everywhere they also report flight, attachment, and arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the land tax and rent levied by the various circuits, though nominally large in quota, often meet flood or drought or encounter insects and frost; among them there is reduction without increase, and everywhere they also report flight, attachment, and arrears.

sentences.zh: 乃至軍儲官俸，常汲汲於供須；

translations.literal: Even military stores and official salaries are constantly urgent in supply;
translations.idiomatic: Even military stores and official salaries are constantly urgent in supply;

sentences.zh: 夏稅秋租，每懸懸於繼續。

translations.literal: summer tax and autumn rent hang ever in suspense for continuation.
translations.idiomatic: summer tax and autumn rent hang ever in suspense for continuation.

sentences.zh: 況今內外倉庫，多是罄空；

translations.literal: Moreover, at present inner and outer storehouses are mostly emptied;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at present inner and outer storehouses are mostly emptied;

sentences.zh: 遠近生民，或聞饑歉。

translations.literal: near and far among the living people one hears of famine and dearth.
translations.idiomatic: near and far among the living people one hears of famine and dearth.

sentences.zh: 伏惟朝廷尚添軍額，更益師徒，非時之博糴難為，異日之區分轉大。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the court still adds military quotas and further increases troops and followers; untimely bulk purchase of grain is hard to accomplish, and the division of burdens on another day will grow greater.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that the court still adds military quotas and further increases troops and followers; untimely bulk purchase of grain is hard to accomplish, and the division of burdens on another day will grow greater.

sentences.zh: 竊慮年支有闕，國計可憂。

translations.literal: I venture to fear that annual expenditure will have gaps and state accounts may be worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to fear that annual expenditure will have gaps and state accounts may be worrisome.

sentences.zh: 望陛下節例外之破除，放諸項以儉省，不添冗食，且止新兵，務急去繁，以寬經費，減奢從儉，漸俟豐盈，則屈者知恩，叛者從化，弭兵有日，富俗可期。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will restrain extraordinary abolitions and releases of various items for frugal saving, not add superfluous consumption, and for the time halt new troops; urgently seek to remove complexity to broaden expenditures, reduce extravagance and follow thrift, and gradually await abundance—then the wronged will know grace, rebels will follow transformation, the cessation of arms will have its day, and a wealthy custom may be expected.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will restrain extraordinary abolitions and releases of various items for frugal saving, not add superfluous consumption, and for the time halt new troops; urgently seek to remove complexity to broaden expenditures, reduce extravagance and follow thrift, and gradually await abundance—then the wronged will know grace, rebels will follow transformation, the cessation of arms will have its day, and a wealthy custom may be expected.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞治民尚清，為政務易，易則煩苛並去，清則偏黨無施。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that governing the people values clarity and conducting government values ease; with ease, vexation and harshness are both removed; with clarity, factional bias is not applied.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that governing the people values clarity and conducting government values ease; with ease, vexation and harshness are both removed; with clarity, factional bias is not applied.

sentences.zh: 若擇其良牧，委在正人，則境內蒸黎，必獲蘇息，官中倉庫，亦絕侵欺。

translations.literal: If one selects good prefects and entrusts them to upright men, then the common people within the borders will surely obtain relief and recovery, and official storehouses will also be free of encroachment and fraud.
translations.idiomatic: If one selects good prefects and entrusts them to upright men, then the common people within the borders will surely obtain relief and recovery, and official storehouses will also be free of encroachment and fraud.

sentences.zh: 伏望誡見在之處官，無乖撫俗；

translations.literal: I humbly hope to admonish the officials now in place not to depart from comforting the people;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope to admonish the officials now in place not to depart from comforting the people;

sentences.zh: 擇將來之蒞事，更審求賢。

translations.literal: in choosing those who will come to office in the future, examine more carefully in seeking the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: in choosing those who will come to office in the future, examine more carefully in seeking the worthy.

sentences.zh: 儻一一得人，則農無所苦；

translations.literal: If in each case one obtains the right man, then farmers will have no suffering;
translations.idiomatic: If in each case one obtains the right man, then farmers will have no suffering;

sentences.zh: 人人致理，則國復何憂。

translations.literal: if every man brings order, then what worry remains for the state?
translations.idiomatic: if every man brings order, then what worry remains for the state?

sentences.zh: 但奉公善政者，不惜重酬；

translations.literal: Only for those who serve the public with good government, do not spare heavy reward;
translations.idiomatic: Only for those who serve the public with good government, do not spare heavy reward;

sentences.zh: 昧理無功者，勿頒厚俸。

translations.literal: Those who are ignorant of principle and without achievement—do not bestow heavy salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are ignorant of principle and without achievement should not receive heavy salaries.

sentences.zh: 益彰有道，兼絕徇情。

translations.literal: Thus the way will be further displayed and partiality to feeling will be wholly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the way will be further displayed and partiality to feeling will be wholly cut off.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下，念臣布露之前言，閔臣驚憂於後患，察臣愚直，杜彼讒邪，臣即但副天心，不防人口，庶幾萬一，仰答聖明。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will recall your servant's earlier words laid bare, pity your servant's alarm and worry over later troubles, perceive your servant's foolish uprightness, and block those slanderers and the wicked—then your servant will only accord with Heaven's heart and not guard against men's mouths, perchance in the slightest degree to answer upward to sagacious clarity.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will recall my earlier words laid bare, pity my alarm and worry over later troubles, perceive my foolish uprightness, and block those slanderers and the wicked—then I will only accord with Heaven's heart and not guard against men's mouths, perchance in the slightest degree to answer upward to sagacious clarity.

sentences.zh: 末帝優詔答之，召於便殿，謂之曰：「卿所論奏，深中時病，形之切言，頗救朕失。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor answered with a gracious edict, summoned him to the informal hall, and said to him, "What you memorialized strikes deep at the ailments of the times; formed in cutting words, it has considerably remedied Our errors.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor answered with a gracious edict, summoned him to the informal hall, and said to him, "What you memorialized strikes deep at the ailments of the times; formed in cutting words, it has considerably remedied Our errors.

sentences.zh: 國計事重，日得商量，無勞過慮也。」

translations.literal: State accounts are weighty affairs; we may consult day by day—no need for excessive worry."
translations.idiomatic: State accounts are weighty affairs; we may consult day by day—no need for excessive worry."

sentences.zh: 延朗不得已而承命。

translations.literal: Yanlang had no choice but to accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang had no choice but to accept the command.

sentences.zh: 延朗有心計，善理繁劇。

translations.literal: Yanlang had schemes in his mind and was skilled at managing complexity.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang was resourceful and skilled at managing complexity.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖在太原，朝廷猜忌，不欲令有積聚，係官財貨留使之外，延朗悉遣取之，晉高祖深銜其事。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu of Jin was at Taiyuan the court was suspicious and did not wish him to accumulate stores; apart from official goods left with the commissioner, Yanlang sent men to take them all, and the Gaozu of Jin deeply resented the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu of Jin was at Taiyuan the court was suspicious and did not wish him to accumulate stores; apart from official goods left with the commissioner, Yanlang sent men to take them all, and the Gaozu of Jin deeply resented the matter.

sentences.zh: 及晉陽起兵，末帝議親征，然亦采浮論，不能果決；

translations.literal: When troops rose at Jinyang the Last Emperor deliberated on a personal campaign, yet he also adopted floating opinion and could not decide firmly;
translations.idiomatic: When troops rose at Jinyang the Last Emperor deliberated on a personal campaign, yet he also adopted floating opinion and could not decide firmly;

sentences.zh: 延朗獨排眾議，請末帝北行，識者韙之。

translations.literal: Yanlang alone rejected the crowd's opinion and asked the Last Emperor to march north—men of insight approved him.
